rondas.inheritedNote: This post uses the company's general rules. On saving, a dedicated configuration will be created just for this post.
rondas.frequencyHint: How often a patrol must be done.
rondas.roundsPerShiftHint: Informational only for now: it's noted as the post's expectation, but it doesn't generate alerts on its own yet. Frequency is what enforces compliance.
rondas.graceHint: Margin before marking a patrol as late.
rondas.maxDurationHint: Maximum time to complete a full patrol.
rondas.requirePhotoHint: The guard must take a date- and time-stamped photo at each point.
rondas.requireGeofenceHint: It checks where the guard is when marking each point.
rondas.geofenceRadiusHint: Maximum distance from the point for the scan to count.
rondas.requireNoteHint: The guard must leave a written note at each point.
rondas.requireOrderHint: The guard must mark the points in the order you defined, not whatever suits them. Check that order first in Posts › Patrols: until now it didn't exist, and the points were numbered by the date they were created.
rondas.notifyStartHint: When a guard starts a patrol.
rondas.emailOnCompleteHint: In addition to the alert, it sends an email to administrators and supervisors (requires email configured).
rondas.notifyMissedHint: When a patrol isn't done or is done out of time.
rondas.notifyClientHint: The post's client receives an alert when the patrol is COMPLETED. Starts and missed patrols are internal: they're never shown to them.
rondas.pageSubtitle: Define the default cadence, validation and notifications for patrols.

emergency.whoReceivesDesc: Push, bell, full-screen alert and email. The same list governs escalation. Include your own roles — a monitoring center can receive everything.
emergency.extraEmailsDesc: Fixed recipients outside your staff (your external monitoring center, a contractor). Comma-separated.
emergency.escaladoDesc: A panic that no one acknowledges keeps alerting until someone attends to it or the time runs out.

guardsGlobal.loadError: The settings could not be loaded.
guardsGlobal.pageSubtitle: These preferences apply to all guards in your company.
guardsGlobal.inactivityHint: Notifies supervisors when an on-duty guard or supervisor stops reporting location (phone off, no signal or app closed). The alert reaches the panel, the apps and via email/SMS according to your notification channels.
guardsGlobal.remindersLabel: Remind guards of their upcoming shifts
guardsGlobal.remindersHint: Automatic alerts before each shift, so no one misses after their rest days.
guardsGlobal.remindersExplain: Each one checked is one message per shift and per guard. With twenty shifts a month, all five come to a hundred messages to each person.
guardsGlobal.aviso_1h_hint: It's usually the only one needed.
guardsGlobal.noneSelected: With none checked, no reminder is sent.
guardsGlobal.messagesPerShift: {{n}} message{{plural}} per shift and per guard.
guardsGlobal.adaptiveHint: A guard with no tardiness or absences in 30 days gets only «1 day before» and «1 hour before»; a repeat offender gets all the active ones. Less noise for those who don't need it — and the alerts mean something again.
guardsGlobal.licenseAlertLabel: Notify when a credential is about to expire
guardsGlobal.licenseAlertHint: HR receives a weekly alert for each credential or license about to expire (or already expired) until it's renewed. Credentials are recorded in each guard's profile.
guardsGlobal.blockClockInLabel: Prevent clocking in with an expired credential
guardsGlobal.blockClockInHint: Until now an expired credential only generated an alert: the guard clocked in anyway, was assigned a post and appeared in the client report. Turn it on only when your credential dates are up to date — otherwise, someone may be left unable to start their shift.
guardsGlobal.performanceHint: Everyone starts at 100 and only goes down for what is actually measured: punctuality, uniform, inventory, standing orders, patrols, tests, training and client rating, plus absences. Turned off, nobody sees a score — not you on their profile, not the officer in their app; it is not set to zero, it stops existing. To stop measuring ONE person, use the switch on their profile, under Performance.

postingGlobal.loadError: The settings could not be loaded.
postingGlobal.saveSuccess: Post rules saved. They apply immediately.
postingGlobal.pageSubtitle: Operational rules applied to all security posts in your company.
postingGlobal.requireActiveShiftLabel: Require an active shift to scan patrols
postingGlobal.requireActiveShiftHint: The guard must have clocked in for a checkpoint scan to count. Prevents patrols recorded off-shift.
postingGlobal.escalateAfterHint: Minutes a post can go uncovered before the alert steps up. It's checked every 5 minutes, so below that the escalation wouldn't give any reaction time.
postingGlobal.geofenceExitLabel: Alert when the guard leaves the geofence
postingGlobal.geofenceExitHint: Using the shift's GPS, it detects when the guard leaves their post's area while on duty and notifies supervisors (requires 2 consecutive readings outside, to avoid GPS false positives). Mobile posts are exempt.
postingGlobal.geofenceReturnHint: Sends a second notification when the guard re-enters the geofence.
postingGlobal.geofenceChannelsPre: Where these alerts arrive (panel, email or SMS) is decided in

appearance.hueHint: What color it is: from red to green, to blue and back.
appearance.intensityHint: How much color it has: from muted gray to full.
appearance.contrastStrong: How light or dark the color turns out, we decide
appearance.contrastRest: , and it's not an oversight: it's what keeps text readable on top of the color, whichever you pick. You set the hue and intensity; we take care of the contrast.
appearance.lightDarkIntro: The same color works in both. Choose the one you work better with — by day in a sunny guard booth, light; in a dark monitoring center, dark.
appearance.darkDesc: Black background, rests your eyes at night
appearance.previewIntro: Real pieces of the platform with the color you just chose. Danger, warning and all-clear notices never change color: a red alert has to stay red even if you pick red as your company's color.

security.passwordsHint: Applies to new passwords and changes. The platform already enforces a minimum that can't be loosened — here you can only tighten it.
security.idleHint: Signs out of the CRM when no one is using it — a reception desk's browser doesn't stay open for a month. The guards' apps aren't affected.
security.platformHint: CGuardPro manages them for all companies. Here you can see whether they're active.

central.loadError: The settings could not be loaded.
central.chooseStationError: Choose which post is the monitoring center: that's what determines who has the console.
central.pageSubtitle: If your company has a 24/7 console: where it is, who can go out to cover and who the alerts reach.
central.hasCentralSection: Do you have a monitoring center?
central.enabledLabel: My company operates a monitoring center
central.enabledHint: With this off nothing changes: updates and alarms are distributed as before, by role.
central.consoleLocationIntro: The monitoring center is just another post. When you choose it, whoever clocks in there is — by definition — the one who has the console, and going out to cover a post becomes normal coverage, not a special case.
central.chooseStationPlaceholder: — Choose the post that is the monitoring center —
central.nobodyClockedIn: Nobody clocked in at the monitoring center
central.operatorsCoverLabel: My operators can go out to cover posts
central.operatorsCoverHint: Turn it on if your console operator sometimes covers a service post: you'll be able to assign them to client posts and the clock will let them choose between the monitoring center and the post. Off, the console is their only place. (In both cases the operator needs a guard role to be able to clock in at the monitoring center: that's what makes it possible to know who has the console.)
central.alertOperatorLabel: Notify whoever has the console first
central.alertOperatorHint: Updates and alarms go to the operator clocked in at the monitoring center, instead of to everyone with the role whether they're asleep or not. If no one is clocked in, notifications go out by role as always: an alert is never left without a recipient.
central.escalateLabel: Escalate to the supervisor if no one responds
central.crmAccessSection: Who gets panel access through the console
central.crmAccessIntro: Assigning a guard to this post opens the company panel for them so they can do console work: handling clock-ins, opening and closing incidents, watching the live map, the cameras and the radio log. They cannot touch settings, users or billing. They keep using their field app, so when they are moved to cover a post they clock in there as usual.
central.crmAccessRevoke: Access follows the assignment: remove them from this post and they stop getting in. There is nothing to revoke by hand.
central.crmAccessEmpty: Nobody is assigned to this post yet, so nobody gets panel access this way. Assign your console operator from Schedule or from the post's page.

retencion.locationTrailDays_queEs: The route guards and supervisors took during their shifts, point by point.
retencion.locationTrailDays_quePierdes: You lose the ability to prove where someone went. Shortening it is also a valid privacy decision: it's the most sensitive data you keep about your people.

retencion.communicationLogsDays_quePierdes: The proof that a notification went out and arrived, and the breakdown of what was charged. It's the fastest-growing record of all.
retencion.auditLogDays_queEs: Who changed what within the platform, and with what values.
retencion.auditLogDays_quePierdes: The answer to «who changed this?». When you need it, you really need it, and it always comes to light too late.

notificationForm.panicButtonHint: It always reaches the phone and this screen, even if you uncheck the box: it's an emergency
notificationForm.coverageUncoveredHint: No one showed up at the post or the guard left it. It reaches the phone even if you uncheck the box
notificationForm.vigiaDigestHint: A summary of the day written by the assistant, at 9 at night — only if there was something to report. Check Email to receive it in your inbox
notificationForm.incidentUnattendedHint: When a critical incident has been open for a while and no one has acknowledged it. It stops insisting as soon as someone takes it
notificationForm.balanceLowHint: With no balance, paid SMS and WhatsApp messages stop being sent, including emergency ones. Email still arrives because it doesn't depend on the balance
notificationForm.panelOfflineHint: The panel stopped signaling that it's alive within the term you set on its record. It also notifies when it comes back
notificationForm.attendanceExceptionsHint: Lateness, absence, early departure, leaving without clocking out, and clocking in outside the geofence
notificationForm.attendanceApprovalsHint: Corrections submitted, pending approval, approved and rejected
notificationForm.contractExpiryHint: Weekly notice before a client's contract expires, with the lead time you set on its record
notificationForm.smsConfirm:
You're about to enable SMS delivery for all {{n}} notifications.

SMS is charged per message and per recipient, and it's deducted from your balance. A frequent notification —like shift check-ins and check-outs— can burn through it fast.

Continue?
notificationForm.quietHoursToggle: Don't send notifications to the phone at night
notificationForm.quietHoursUrgentText: panic button, absence, abandoned post, inactive guard and escalations. The silence is for the noise — tasks, reminders and informational notices. And it only affects the phone: you still receive the dashboard and email, so they're there when you wake up.
notificationForm.channelsIntro: Check which channel you want each notification on. The header checkbox turns an entire channel on or off; the one on each row, all channels for that notification.
notificationForm.rondasMiddle: —completed, missed, started— aren't controlled here, but in

wa.pitch: Connect your company's WhatsApp. Your clients keep messaging your current number — there's no need to change numbers.
wa.disconnectDesc: The platform will stop sending WhatsApp messages with your number. You can reconnect it whenever you want — your number and your Meta account aren't affected.

comms.rechargeSuccess: Payment received. Your balance will update in a few seconds.
comms.walletHint: Prepaid balance for SMS. WhatsApp is billed directly to your Meta account when you connect it.
comms.walletHint2: A single prepaid balance for SMS (Twilio), WhatsApp templates, and the VigIA assistant.
comms.noBalance: You've run out of balance. Messages with a cost won't go out until you top up.
comms.lowBalance: Low balance: below the configured threshold. Channels with a cost may be blocked.
comms.rechargeHint: Secure card payment via Stripe. The balance is credited automatically once the payment is confirmed and covers the SMS sent by the platform.
comms.smsFallbackDesc: Use SMS (Twilio) when push and WhatsApp aren't available.
comms.smsCriticalDesc: Sends SMS for visitor and patrol alerts. The panic button always sends SMS, independent of this.
comms.criticalSmsFallbackDesc: Allows backup SMS when a critical alert isn't delivered.
comms.walletRequired: Require balance for channels with a cost
comms.walletRequiredDesc: Blocks SMS sending when there isn't enough balance.
comms.whatsappEnabledDesc: Sends messages from your own WhatsApp Business (billed by Meta to your company).
comms.whatsappShiftRemindersDesc: Notifies shifts by WhatsApp if the guard doesn't have push.
comms.whatsappIncidentsDesc: Alerts supervisors and administrators by WhatsApp.
comms.orderHint: Each notification tries the cheapest channel first and only moves to the next if it doesn't arrive.
comms.otpChannel: Preferred channel for the access code
comms.noLogs: No records for the applied filters.
comms.noLogsDesc: Change or clear the filters to see more sends.
